'''María Luisa''' ('''Marisa''') '''Fernández Rodríguez''' (11 June 1953 - 18 November 2025){{r|born}} was a Spanish mathematician specializing in [[differential geometry]], [[symplectic geometry]], and [[G2-structure|{{math|''G''<sub>2</sub>}}-structures]].{{r|nuve}} She was professor of geometry and topology in the department of mathematics at the [[University of the Basque Country]].{{r|elp}}

==Education and career==
Fernández was originally from [[Ourense]].{{r|nuve}} She was a mathematics student at the [[University of Santiago de Compostela]], earning a [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] there in 1974 and completing her doctorate in 1976.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Estructura y propiedades de las variedades G1'', was supervised by {{ill|Enrique Vidal Abascal|es}}.{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research with [[Alfred Gray (mathematician)|Alfred Gray]] at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], she joined the faculty of science at the University of the Basque Country in 1986.{{r|nuve}}

She died on 18 November 2025.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=In memoriam de la Prof. Marisa Fernández|url=https://matematicas.ucm.es/noticias/la-facultad-de-cc-matematicas-lamenta-el-fallecimiento-de-la-prof-marisa-fernandez|website=[[Universidad Complutense de Madrid]]|access-date=2025-12-01|language=es|trans-title=In memoriam of Prof. Marisa Fernández}}</ref> 

==Recognition==
In 1988, the government of the [[Province of Pontevedra]] gave Fernández the Antonio Odriozola Prize for basic research.{{r|nuve}} She was a 2019 winner of the medal of the [[Royal Spanish Mathematical Society]].{{r|nuve|elp}}

== Research ==
Fernández made influential contributions to differential and symplectic geometry, often working at the interface with topology.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Fernández-Rodríguez, Mª Luisa|url=https://gadeaciencia.org/team-members/fernandez-rodriguez-ma-luisa/|access-date=2025-12-01|language=es|website=Fundación Gadea Ciencia}}</ref>

Together with Gray and Gotay, she provided the first example of a [[symplectic manifold]] which does not admit a compatible complex structure, hence cannot be [[Kähler manifold|Kähler]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Compact Parallelizable Four Dimensional Symplectic and Complex Manifolds|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2047114|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=1988|pages=1209|volume=103|issue=4|doi=10.2307/2047114|first1=Marisa|last1=Fernández|first2=Mark J.|last2=Gotay|first3=Alfred|last3=Gray|author-link3=Alfred Gray (mathematician)|author-link1=Marisa Fernández| jstor=2047114 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Together with Vicente Muñoz, she resolved a question posed by Babenko and Taimanov by providing the first example of a [[Compact space|compact]], [[Simply connected space|simply connected]] symplectic manifold that is nonformal in the sense of [[rational homotopy theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=An 8-dimensional nonformal, simply connected, symplectic manifold|url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2008/167-3/p08|doi=10.4007/annals.2008.167.1045|language=en-US|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|last1=Fernández|first1=Marisa|date=2008|volume=167|pages=1045–1054|last2=Muñoz|first2=Vicente |issue=3 }}</ref> Their construction has become a landmark result in symplectic topology and significantly advanced the understanding of the homotopical properties of symplectic manifolds.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
